title: The Ungrateful Guest
attribution: Excerpted (trimmed) from "The Ungrateful Guest" in Fifty Famous Stories Retold by James Baldwin (1896), via Project Gutenberg. One sentence of background has been trimmed, and the syllable-break hyphen in the original edition's "treat-ment" has been corrected.
body: Among the soldiers of King Philip there was a poor man who had done some brave deeds.

One day this soldier was on board of a ship at sea when a great storm came up. The winds drove the ship upon the rocks, and it was wrecked. The soldier was cast half-drowned upon the shore; and he would have died there, had it not been for the kind care of a farmer who lived close by.
When the soldier was well enough to go home, he thanked the farmer for what he had done, and promised that he would repay him for his kindness.

But he did not mean to keep his promise. He did not tell King Philip about the man who had saved his life. He only said that there was a fine farm by the seashore, and that he would like very much to have it for his own. Would the king give it to him?
"Who owns the farm now?" asked Philip.
"Only a churlish farmer, who has never done anything for his country," said the soldier.
"Very well, then," said Philip. "You have served me for a long time, and you shall have your wish. Go and take the farm for yourself."
And so the soldier made haste to drive the farmer from his house and home. He took the farm for his own.

The poor farmer was stung to the heart by such treatment. He went boldly to the king, and told the whole story from beginning to end. King Philip was very angry when he learned that the man whom he had trusted had done so base a deed. He sent for the soldier in great haste; and when he had come, he caused these words to be burned in his forehead:
Thus all the world was made to know of the mean act by which the soldier had tried to enrich himself; and from that day until he died all men shunned and hated him.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happens to the soldier's ship at sea?
options: It is captured by enemy sailors
It runs out of food before reaching shore
A storm drives it onto the rocks and wrecks it
It is sold by the soldier for gold

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who saves the soldier's life after the shipwreck?
options: A farmer who lived close by
Another soldier from his unit
A fisherman passing in his boat
King Philip's own guards

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the soldier promise the farmer once he recovers?
options: That he would send his son to help on the farm
That he would introduce him to King Philip
That he would give him a share of his pay
That he would repay him for his kindness

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the soldier actually ask King Philip for?
options: A ship to replace the one he lost
The fine farm by the seashore, for his own
A reward of gold for his service
Permission to retire from the army

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the soldier describe the farmer to King Philip?
options: As a brave man who saved his life at sea
As an old friend from before the war
As a churlish man who has never done anything for his country
As a dishonest man who cheats his neighbors

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does King Philip do once he learns the whole story?
options: He has the words "The Ungrateful Guest" burned into the soldier's forehead
He orders the soldier to return the farm quietly
He exiles the soldier from the kingdom
He forgives the soldier and asks him to repay the farmer

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how do people treat the soldier for the rest of his life?
options: They pitied him and forgave his mistake
They admired his cleverness in gaining the farm
They forgot the story within a few years
All men shunned and hated him

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the soldier hide the farmer's identity from King Philip?
options: He has genuinely forgotten who saved his life
He knows the truth would prevent the king from giving him the farm
He wants to protect the farmer from unwanted attention
He believes the king already knows the whole story

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why is King Philip especially angry when he learns the truth?
options: He had wanted the farm for himself all along
He disliked the farmer even before hearing the story
He had trusted the soldier and been deceived into wronging his rescuer
He had already given the farm to someone else

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "churlish" mean, as the soldier falsely applies it to the farmer?
options: Rude and unhelpful
Wealthy and generous
Young and inexperienced
Brave and loyal

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what kind of man was the soldier before the shipwreck?
options: A wealthy landowner near the coast
A stranger newly arrived in the kingdom
A farmer who later joined the army
A poor man who had done some brave deeds

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the soldier do once he is well enough to go home?
options: He leaves without saying a word to the farmer
He thanks the farmer and promises to repay him
He asks the farmer to join him in the army
He pays the farmer immediately in coin

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the farmer do once he is driven from his home?
options: He quietly moves to a new farm elsewhere
He asks the soldier's family for help
He goes boldly to the king and tells the whole story
He gives up and lives without a home

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does King Philip grant the soldier's request so easily at first?
options: He believes the soldier's false description of the farmer and trusts his long service
He had already decided to give away that farm before the soldier asked
He owed the farmer a debt and wanted to settle it
He wanted to test whether the soldier was being honest

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the burned inscription on the soldier's forehead accomplish?
options: It cures him of his desire for land and wealth
It warns other soldiers never to go to sea again
It restores the farm to the farmer immediately
It makes his shameful act known to everyone he meets afterward

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that people "shunned" the soldier afterward?
options: They frequently visited him
They deliberately avoided him
They admired him from a distance
They forgot who he was

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A soldier is shipwrecked and never recovers from his injuries
A farmer steals land from the soldier who once saved him
A soldier repays his rescuer's kindness with betrayal, and is publicly shamed for it
A king refuses to believe a farmer's complaint against a soldier
